interest: U.S. liner's encounter with Japanese fleet maneuvers, 1941.
overview: 1941 consular reports on Japanese naval maneuvers closing the Inland Sea and a liner's encounter with a carrier force.

people.name: Addison E. Southard
people.role: American Consul General at Hong Kong

subfiles.about: Reports the prohibition of foreigners from traveling on the Inland Sea due to Japanese naval maneuvers.
subfiles.summary: Sokobin reports foreigners barred from the Inland Sea, February 15–25, 1941, for naval maneuvers.
subfiles.title: Telegram from Sokobin (Kobe) on Inland Sea Travel Restrictions

subfiles.about: A confidential paraphrase of the February 20 telegram from Kobe regarding travel prohibitions on the Inland Sea.
subfiles.from: Division of Far Eastern Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Paraphrase of Kobe telegram on the Inland Sea ban for maneuvers.
subfiles.title: Paraphrase of Kobe Telegram on Inland Sea Naval Maneuvers
subfiles.to: Office of Naval Intelligence and Military Intelligence Division

subfiles.about: Transmits a memorandum detailing an American missionary's observation of Japanese warships conducting maneuvers near Kobe.
subfiles.from: Addison E. Southard (American Consul General, Hong Kong)
subfiles.summary: Southard forwards Bruins's memo on Japanese maneuvers seen from the President Cleveland.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 874 from Southard (Hong Kong) on Japanese War Vessels Observed in Maneuvers

subfiles.about: Memorandum recording Rev. Walter de Velder's account of sighting Japanese naval maneuvers from the S.S. President Cleveland.
subfiles.from: John H. Bruins (American Consul, Hong Kong)
subfiles.summary: Bruins reports a missionary's account of Japanese warships laying a smoke screen when the President Cleveland refused to change course.
subfiles.title: Memorandum by Bruins on Movements of Japanese Naval Vessels
subfiles.to: Addison E. Southard (American Consul General, Hong Kong)
